newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk private banks' 96 short fx positions at $2.6.
newsitem.headline: Turk private banks' 96 short fx positions at $2.6.

text.p: Turkey's 33 private banks carried short foreign currency positions totalling $2.57 billion at the end of 1996, up 15.3 percent from $2.23 billion in 1995, a treasury report said.

It said big private banks had $1.37 billion, medium-size banks had $943 million and small ones held $243 million of short currency positions mainly due to expectations of lower lira depreciation and higher returns on Turkish lira placements.

"The economic policies and their effects on the markets encourage banks to run short foreign currency positions," the report said, warning against rising short positions which it said neared the levels seen before the 1994 financial crisis.

"Continuous financing of Turkish lira funds by maintaining high levels of short currency positions may produce negative results in the currency market especially when economic and political uncertainties exist and foreign currency reserves are not sufficient," it added.
-- Hatice Aydogdu, Ankara newsroom +90-212-275 08 75 ATA EKS
